transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Holt (Redwood SE); Liam Carter, Sofia Alvarez, Priam Bhandari, Grace Foley (Northstar)

Summary: exploratory discovery to understand Northstar's constraints around keystore residency, log flows, and whether Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments fit their audit and latency requirements. Customer is heavily regulated (investment mgmt) and needs evidence trails and strong KMS residency guarantees.

00:00:12 Jordan Ellis: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round of intros, i'm jordan with redwood, ae. priya and marcus here are our se team.
00:00:22 Liam Carter: hi, liam carter, head of cloud at northstar.
00:00:25 Sofia Alvarez: sofia, ciso. 
00:00:27 Priam Bhandari: pri am, platform eng. grace from legal will join for parts.
00:00:33 Jordan: high level we want to understand your must-haves, like where keys must live, log retention, who can access raw transcripts, and if a private deployment is required. 
00:00:46 Sofia: critical things for us: keys must be in our KMS, nothing leaves eu for eu customers, audit logs must show request/response hashes and we need proof of deletion for legal hold. also sock two and iso stuff.
00:01:05 Priya Nair: got it — for clarity when you say keys in your kms do you mean HSM-backed aws kms with customer-managed key or physically separate hsm?
00:01:17 Sofia: we require customer-managed KMS with key material never exported. HSM is preferred especially for certain fund types.
00:01:29 Marcus Holt: okay that points us toward either dedicated capacity with KMS integration or the private deployment where the control plane is customer VPC — both can be configured to use your KMS. hosted api also supports cx-managed keys but not full key material residency.
00:01:48 Priam: latency wise we need 95th percentile under 220ms for our 512 token flows, otherwise it impacts UIs. do we have numbers for hosted vs dedicated?
00:02:00 Jordan: quick note — our public benchmarks for similar configs are in the deck we shared, but numbers vary by sequence length and batching. hosted can hit sub-200ms for small prompt profiles; dedicated is more predictable. i'll send the spreadsheet.
00:02:16 Liam: what's the tradeoff on logs? we don't want raw outputs stored in your telemetry.
00:02:23 Priya: yes we can toggle telemetry. there's a log-minimization mode that strips response bodies and only stores metadata, or you can opt into full retention for debugging under an SLA.
00:02:36 Sofia: legal will want the retention windows and who sees the logs, plus the ability to request complete purge for user data. also questions about subpoena handling across borders.
00:02:48 Grace Foley: to add, we need contract language that says we control export keys and that redwood won't access raw data without a court order and appropriate legal process.
00:03:02 Marcus: understood. in private deployments the data plane and logs stay in your VPC and we only see aggregated metrics via ops hooks. in dedicated we can enforce tenant isolation with customer key references. hosted is the only mode where some telemetry may cross our control plane unless you pick the privacy tier.
00:03:24 Jordan: can you walk us through a sample request flow so we can map the logs and keystore hops?
00:03:31 Priam: sure — client -> our edge -> request with customer id header -> redwood endpoint -> model. we want the model's kv cache not to persist to external stores and any logs to be redacted.
00:03:46 Priya: note: kv cache is in-memory and managed on the runtime. it doesn't write model internals to persistent object stores unless you enable long-term caching. sometimes transcriptions mis-say K V cash as K V cache, we've seen that in transcripts :).
00:04:02 Sofia: there was mention of fallback routing — if eu region is saturated can you route to a fallback region? we need to know how jurisdictional reads are handled.
00:04:13 Marcus: yes, we have routing policies: region-lock, region-prefer, and region-fallback. region-fallback will route to a queued compatible model in another region. for regulated traffic, we'd recommend region-lock or dedicated capacity with reserved throughput.
00:04:30 Liam: how is audit evidence produced? we need immutable logs, signed entries, and a chain-of-custody report.
00:04:39 Priya: our control plane can emit signed audit logs (log signing) that include request id, timestamp, model version, and access decision. for private deployments those logs live in your cloud buckets and you own keys. for hosted we can provide export bundles and attestation.
00:04:56 Sofia: are there known limits for log export size? we deal with a lot of volume during EOD recons.
00:05:03 Jordan: export is configurable; we typically recommend pushing structured event streams to a customer-managed kafka or s3 bucket with lifecycle rules. we can compress and batch.
00:05:15 Priam: on encryption at rest, does redwood encrypt model cache and artifacts with your master keys or the customer's?
00:05:23 Marcus: by default the runtime encrypts caches with service-managed keys, but in dedicated/private we support envelope encryption with your KMS keys so the key never leaves your control.
00:05:36 Grace: legal question: how do you handle legal holds for a single investor? we need the ability to freeze and produce all interactions for a given investor id.
00:05:47 Priya: we can tie request-level metadata to your user ids and mark retention flags. in private/dedicated you control retention policies; we can surface an API call to 'lock' records pending legal hold.
00:06:02 Liam: let's talk about PII redaction — we'd like automatic redaction and also the ability to run our own scrubber pre-send. which is better?
00:06:12 Priya: both are supported. pre-send scrubbing in your infra is the strictest approach. we also offer built-in redaction at the ingestion layer; note though built-in redaction can increase latency by ~40-80ms depending on rules.
00:06:27 Jordan: could you clarify the acceptable latency increase?
00:06:29 Priam: up to 50ms is acceptable on average, spikes okay if below 220ms p95.
00:06:36 Marcus: for the pilot we'll measure baseline and then enable redaction to show delta.
00:06:42 Sofia: compliance checklist: SOC2, ISO 27001, GDPR data subject access request (DSAR) process, HIPAA for a specific fund that handles health-related securities — can you support the HIPAA overlap?
00:06:57 Priya: we have customers running hipaa-bound workflows. hosted may require a BAA with additional controls; dedicated/private are easier to certify. we can share the BAA template.
00:07:09 Grace: how about personnel access — who at redwood can read raw, unredacted request/response? need RBAC and audit of reader sessions.
00:07:18 Marcus: role-based access with timebound justification is supported. access to production request payloads is limited to named on-call roles and must be explicitly approved; all such sessions are audited and recorded.
00:07:32 Jordan: can you walk through an incident response scenario where a customer requests deletion or a breach occurs?
00:07:38 Priya: typical steps: containment (stop ingestion), preserve logs, run forensics in your VPC if private, rotate keys, and coordinate disclosure. we will standby and provide artifacts. for hosted we have a documented IR runbook and can assist with customer-specific playbooks.
00:07:55 Sofia: does redwood run analytics or training on customer telemetry?
00:08:00 Jordan: no training on customer data by default; telemetry aggregated for service improvement can be opted-out. any usage for product improvement is anonymized and we can exclude accounts.
00:08:12 Liam: what about cross-border subpoenas — if data is routed outside eu, how is that handled?
00:08:20 Marcus: that is a legal question; operationally, region-lock prevents routing outside the region. if you allow fallback, then we recommend adding contractual protections and geo-fencing controls.
00:08:33 Priam: for the pilot we want: 1) hosted baseline, 2) dedicated capacity with our KMS, and 3) private control plane in our VPC for the most sensitive funds. 
00:08:45 Jordan: great — that gives us three tracks for the bake-off. we'll produce configs and expected costs.
00:08:50 Grace: on contracts, we will need the data processing addendum and an explicit keystore residency clause.
00:08:58 Jordan: noted.
00:09:05 [---interruption 00:09:05 audio glitch---]
00:09:30 Priya: quick technical note: when we talk about keystore routing, the runtime supports both direct KMS calls and a key-proxy pattern. key-proxy allows you to keep HSM behind your firewall and the runtime forwards key ops without persisting material. we documented a pattern for this.
00:09:52 Liam: do you support customer-managed HSM (imported key material) for the private deployment?
00:09:58 Marcus: yes, private supports HSM and can be deployed on-prem if needed. dedicated in cloud supports BYOK with HSM-backed KMS in major clouds.
00:10:08 Sofia: what about long-term audit evidence? we need signed snapshots monthly and a chain of custody for a 7-year retention for certain funds.
00:10:18 Jordan: we can export monthly signed snapshots and integrate with your WORM storage. we'll need to define the signed log format; we typically use RFC-compliant signing with SHA-256 and a signing key reference.
00:10:31 Priam: last thing — billing and cost transparency: we need token-level breakdown and per-route cost. can we get sample invoices?
00:10:39 Jordan: yes we'll provide sample billing with per-route/per-model breakdowns; also cost control hooks to cap spend per route.
00:10:47 Sofia: any open security gaps we should be concerned about?
00:10:51 Priya: the common gap is forgetting to enable region-lock and leaving default telemetry on. also not applying envelope encryption for runtime caches in shared infra. we'll flag those in the post-call notes.
00:11:05 Liam: okay, let's go deeper on the private deployment architecture.
00:11:10 Marcus: i'll share a diagram but high level: control plane can be run as a managed service or self-hosted; data plane sits in your VPC; we deploy agents that pull model artifacts if allowed or you can host model artifacts in a private registry. network egress is controlled via customer security groups.
00:11:29 Priam: about model artifacts — we need assurance that model weights are scanned and provenance is recorded.
00:11:36 Priya: model provenance is captured at onboarding — hash, source, version, and any quantization applied. we keep that in the release manifest.
00:11:46 Sofia: what about dev/test separation? we can't have dev models accidentally routed to prod.
00:11:51 Jordan: we support environment tags, route-level policies, and separate deployments for dev, staging, prod. access tokens can be scoped per environment.
00:12:02 Liam: are there customers doing similar HIPAA+EU mixes? curious about playbooks.
00:12:07 Priya: yes, we've worked with medtech and financials with similar overlap. one reference is a european insurer we can anonymize. i'll add that to the security pack.
00:12:18 Grace: legal will need to review evidence of data deletion processes and the exact wording for keystore residency.
00:12:25 Jordan: we'll include DPA language snippets.
00:12:30 [00:12:30 timestamp — moving to deeper Q&A] 
00:12:32 Priam: technical Q: if a model variant is incompatible across regions (quantized vs fp16), how does fallback maintain parity?
00:12:41 Marcus: good question. we maintain model compatibility mapping and version pinning. fallback will pick a compatible variant with equivalent semantic behavior; we also compute quality heuristics and if a big delta is expected we can fail closed rather than fallback.
00:12:58 Liam: what's the runbook for rollback on model regressions?
00:13:03 Priya: our rollout supports canary, A/B, and instant rollbacks tied to evals. you can pin a previous version per-route. audit trail captures rollout steps.
00:13:12 Sofia: on SSO and identity, we use SAML enterprise SSO and SCIM for provisioning. integrations?
00:13:19 Jordan: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, and SCIM provisioning. role sync can be automated so that engineers are only provisioned into our console with least privilege.
00:13:30 Priam: any extra notes on how debug access is handled with private deployments?
00:13:34 Marcus: debug access is via bastion jump with session recording and ephemeral certs. in private deployment those controls map to your identity provider.
00:13:45 Sofia: is there a standard SLA for dedicated? we need 99.9 for uptime and percentile latency targets.
00:13:52 Jordan: our dedicated offering typically has a 99.9 uptime commitment with latency SLOs defined per commit level. we'll surface the SLA draft.
00:14:02 Liam: ok let's outline the pilot acceptance criteria so we can move quickly.
00:14:06 Jordan: proposed acceptance criteria: 1) p95 latency under 220ms for sample 512-token prompts; 2) KMS key material not exported (attested) and audit logs exported to your s3; 3) redaction pipeline works with <50ms delta; 4) signed monthly snapshots exported; 5) confirmation of no training on customer data.
00:14:27 Priam: that sounds right. can you include throughput targets? we expect 150 RPS sustained for certain routes.
00:14:34 Marcus: we'll include 150 RPS profile and a spike test for 500 RPS.
00:14:40 Grace: legal wants a simple keystore clause we can start with.
00:14:44 Jordan: we'll add a keystore residency clause and DPA snippet into the pack.
00:14:49 [00:14:49 — crosstalk, phone background noise]
00:15:12 Priya: quick aside — sometimes transcripts from fireflies mislabel brand names; we use 'Redwood Dedicated' 'Redwood Private' and 'Redwood Hosted' internally.
00:15:25 Liam: fair. i think we're ready to run the three-track pilot. timeline: kickoff next week?
00:15:30 Jordan: we can kickoff the pilot on 2027-06-14, assuming we exchange artifacts this week.
00:15:36 Sofia: legal review may take 10 business days for the DPA.
00:15:39 Jordan: understood, we'll push the pack asap to accelerate that.
00:15:45 [closing recap] 
00:15:47 Jordan: recap: jordan will share security pack (SOC2/ISO/Baa draft), priya will prepare pilot configs for hosted/dedicated/private and run initial perf expectations, marcus will attach architecture diagrams for private deployment and keystore proxy pattern, priam will send redacted logs and throughput profile, grace/legal will review DPA language.
00:16:10 Grace: yes that's correct.
00:16:13 Liam: thanks all.
00:16:15 Sofia: thanks, bye.

Post-call quick notes:
- Risks flagged: default telemetry left on; non-encrypted runtime cache in hosted.
- Recommended pilot: three parallel tracks with same prompts to compare latency, cost, and evidence exportability.
- Links shared during call: Deck (residency playbook) https://redwood.example/sales/residency-playbook.pdf ; Benchmarks spreadsheet (sample) https://redwood.example/sales/benchmarks-nsam-2027.xlsx ; Security pack placeholder https://redwood.example/sales/security-pack.zip

End of transcript.
